correctness.rationale: For the fixed-n Kingman process with unit rate per unordered pair, the falling factorial moments follow by avoiding r tagged leaves in each merger down to level k. Conditioning on a cherry at step j uses a size bias by (B_j)_2, followed by removal of its two singleton children and uniform-pair survival of the other singletons. For j at or below k, propagating each candidate pair from k to j gives the other mixed-moment term. Summation yields the stated Cov(C_n,B_k), including k=2 and k=n; independent holding times cancel the k(k-1) factor. The remaining sum of m(m-1) from 0 to n-2 is (n-1)(n-2)(n-3)/3, giving -2/9. The cases n=2,3 have one cherry almost surely. This is external, not total tree length; changing the pair rate to beta scales the length covariance by 1/beta. The supplied Python verifier was inspected, not executed. A separate exact Markov calculation over level, singleton count and accumulated cherries checked n=2–8 and all 59 levels at n=60; replay at /workspace/branches/ffce9c23-6d79-44d8-a076-d828d732c8d4/replay_small.py and outputs replay_small.out and replay_60.out. Those finite checks corroborate rather than establish the universal proof.
